thesis: JPMorgan reports ASML customers are already booking EUV lithography capacity for 2028 and management is weighing another 30% capacity expansion, while Third Point disclosed more than doubling its ASML stake in Q2 — signs AI-driven demand for advanced chipmaking tools remains intact. That said, shares are still well off their September highs after the Amodei AI-slowdown commentary triggered a broad chip-sector selloff, and an ASML executive separately warned Europe risks falling behind on chip investment, so the pullback reads as sector-wide sentiment risk rather than a company-specific problem.
invalidation: Confirmed pushouts or cancellations of already-booked 2027/2028 EUV tool orders from major customers such as TSMC, Samsung, or Intel

thesis: TMO beat Q2 estimates on July 23 and raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $24.93-$25.33 and sales guidance to $47.40B-$48.10B, with the CEO citing strengthening customer activity; shares hit a fresh all-time high of $681.55 today, and Goldman ($780), HSBC ($690), and Baird ($686) have all lifted price targets since the print. One Benzinga screen flagged TMO as technically overbought (RSI 71.7 on Sept 22), but that reading looks like sustained fundamental buying following a beat-and-raise quarter rather than speculative froth, so it doesn't change the read.
invalidation: Q3 results or guidance that fail to confirm the raised full-year outlook, or evidence the life-sciences/bioprocessing recovery cited by management is stalling

thesis: Lumentum is riding genuine AI-datacenter optical-interconnect demand — it announced a new high-capacity DWDM laser module for AI systems and will showcase a co-packaged optics demo with Qualcomm and Corning at ECOC — but part of the 60-day gain, including an 8.2% single-day pop on Sept 16, came from a sector-wide sympathy rally after peer Ciena's long-term targets, which one report described as 'short covering after a brutal month for the group' rather than LITE-specific news. Recurring insider sales by the President of Global Business Units (four separate ~$1.3-1.4M sales since mid-September) are a minor watch item but not disqualifying on their own.
invalidation: A slowdown in hyperscaler optical-component orders or a pull-back in AI datacenter capex commitments from LITE's named customers

thesis: Oracle issued a force majeure notice to the developer of its Project Jupiter data center (a Blue Owl Capital unit) seeking to defer payments if the New Mexico site's 2028 target slips — the site's gas pipeline is already delayed to Feb 2027. Oracle says the project 'remains on schedule' and calls the notice routine, but the market didn't buy the reassurance, sending shares down roughly 4% alongside sympathy selling in Dell, Arm, and Bloom Energy. The move also coincides with a broad tech selloff as the 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since 2007, so macro rate pressure is compounding the company-specific dispute.
invalidation: n/a — avoid, not a held position

thesis: UBS shares have sold off after the Swiss Parliament's Council of States backed tighter capital rules that would force UBS to back foreign units with 90% CET1 capital — roughly $16B of additional capital by the company's own estimate, on top of about $15B already required post-Credit Suisse. UBS calls the outcome 'excessive' and management is still pushing back, but the bill still needs the lower house and a final decision isn't expected until next year, so this is a real but still-unresolved regulatory overhang rather than a settled negative.

thesis: Nebius disclosed it will raise on-demand AI compute prices roughly 17-25% across Nvidia GPU, AMD CPU, and memory rentals effective Oct 1, and BNP Paribas upgraded the stock to Outperform (target to $399 from $260) citing that pricing power — both real, already-announced developments rather than analyst speculation about future events. The clearest counter-case is Michael Burry's disclosed short position (part of a broader memory-oversupply short basket alongside Micron and the SOXX ETF) and Rothschild's Sell initiation at $84, but Burry's stated thesis targets memory-chip oversupply from rising Chinese DRAM capacity — a different exposure than Nebius's GPU-cloud rental business, where a company raising its own prices because it's supply-constrained is the opposite signal from an oversupply call, so that short thesis doesn't apply directly here.
invalidation: Confirmation that the announced Oct 1 price increases are delayed, scaled back, or fail to convert into contracted revenue, or evidence of a slowdown in GPU-cloud utilization
